{"schema":"voice-draft-source/4","kind":"draft","draft":"The proposed AI service promises a useful result: shorter intake notes for tomorrow’s meeting. The concealed problem is that confidential client histories must leave the nonprofit’s control before the summary comes back—unless the tool runs inside an environment the organization controls.

Our recommendation is simple: don’t put real intake notes into a general-purpose AI service tomorrow. A confidentiality promise is not enough. The service’s data-processing terms (including retention and deletion), security controls (including access logs and encryption), and contract (including breach notice and vendor responsibility) all need review. If those points aren’t settled in writing, treat the system as outside the confidential case file—not as a clever extension of it.

For tomorrow’s meeting, take a two-track proposal. First, use invented or thoroughly de-identified sample notes to test whether the summaries are accurate, useful, and appropriately limited (remove names, dates, locations, rare circumstances, and identifying quotations). Second, assign one person to complete a short vendor review: Where is the text processed, is it retained, and can humans or subcontractors access it? Will the provider use it to train models? The answers should come from the contract and settings, not from a sales page.

A pilot may reveal administrative value, especially if staff spend less time rewriting routine material. It could also turn a stack of private conversations into a vendor’s searchable vault. That tradeoff should be decided deliberately, before convenience becomes practice.

Approve only a sandboxed test with fictional material tomorrow. Before any live use, require written approval from whoever owns privacy and security decisions, a signed data-processing agreement (DPA), minimum necessary fields, staff access limits, and human review of every summary. If the provider can’t meet those conditions, choose local summarization or ordinary staff notes. We should adopt the tool only when client confidentiality remains the controlling standard.","omitted":[],"refused":""}
